item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q023_homeodomain_heterogeneous_fold","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, d1p7jd_ is domain sunid 94286 for 1p7j chain D and d1ztra1 is domain sunid 125655 for 1ztr chain A residues 0-59. Both resolve to the same species node, Fruit fly / Drosophila melanogaster, under Engrailed Homeodomain, under the Homeodomain family a.4.1.1, whose parent is the Homeodomain-like superfamily a.4.1, then the DNA/RNA-binding 3-helical bundle fold a.4, then the All alpha proteins class a. Thus the family-level classification still justifies the strong homology statement: these two domains are classified as homologous Engrailed homeodomain sequences, not merely as proteins with the same class, fold, or broad superfamily geometry. The caveat is structural. SCOPe annotates d1ztra1 itself with the domain-local inconsistency hf, defined as a heterogeneous-fold case in which a domain adopts a different fold from the exemplar domain while retaining similar sequence and number of secondary structures; d1p7jd_ has no corresponding heterogeneity flag. The PDB metadata also identifies both entries as mutants, with 1p7j described as an Engrailed homeodomain K52E crystal structure complexed with DNA and 1ztr as an Engrailed homeodomain L16A solution structure. Therefore it is justified to transfer evolutionary membership within the Homeodomain family, but not to treat the d1ztra1 coordinates as an interchangeable representative of the canonical a.4 homeodomain fold, as a routine template for d1p7jd_, or as an unqualified same-fold positive in training or evaluation.
